# BLO-35720 — size the prompt Secret cutover against the kernel exec limit, not the PodSpec limit

Changed files:

- `src/server/job-manifest.ts` — `LARGE_PROMPT_THRESHOLD_BYTES` is now derived
  from `MAX_ARG_STRLEN_BYTES` minus the env name, the `=` and the trailing NUL
  (131056), instead of the hand-picked 256 KiB. The env var name is now a shared
  constant, so the length the threshold subtracts cannot drift from the name the
  manifest actually writes.
- `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts` — a parameterised invariant that no prompt
  taking the env path can produce an env string past `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`.

## Why

The old threshold was 256 KiB, chosen to protect against the ~1 MiB PodSpec
limit. But the binding constraint is the Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` =
`32 * PAGE_SIZE` = 131072 bytes, which caps a **single** execve environment
string — including the `NAME=` prefix and the trailing NUL.

So every prompt in the 128 KiB..256 KiB dead zone took the env-var path and was
handed to the `write-prompt` init container's `sh -c` as a string it could not
exec (`E2BIG`). The kubelet surfaced that as a bare non-zero init-container exit
naming neither the prompt nor its size, and Paperclip relabelled it
`k8s_pod_schedule_failed`
([BLO-33503](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-33503)) — so the one
failure mode that is deterministic in prompt size presented as a cluster
capacity problem.

Measured on the `Agent health & stalled-issue check` routine: 10/10 runs dead at
`write-prompt` with `usageJson: null` against a 5.7% background rate, body
135,038 B — inside the dead zone.

The comparison was already `Buffer.byteLength(prompt, "utf-8")`, so a multi-byte
prompt is measured in the units the kernel counts.

## On the tests

The new case covers the dead zone the previous tests skipped entirely — they
exercised only ~0 KiB and 300 KiB, which is why a 100%-reproducible failure had
no failing test. Reverting the threshold alone turns 4 of them red.

No upstream change: this is Paperclip-local code under `src/server/`, not a
carried patch against an upstream adapter release.
